topic_summary: The Non-resident Landlord (NRL) Scheme requires UK tenants and letting agents to deduct basic-rate Income Tax from rent paid to landlords who live abroad for more than 6 months of the year, and to pay that tax to HMRC quarterly within 30 days of each quarter end. This menu routes users to the specific outcome, explainer, or guidance dish that matches their situation.

terminals.heading: I am a tenant paying rent to a landlord who lives abroad — what must I do?
terminals.result_copy: Indicated position: where your landlord lives abroad for more than 6 months of the year and no letting agent is collecting rent, you as tenant are indicated to be required to deduct basic-rate Income Tax at 20% from the rent and pay it to HMRC within 30 days of the end of each tax quarter. You are also indicated to be required to keep records for 4 years. Review recommended to confirm your specific circumstances with HMRC.

terminals.heading: I only found the tenant and collected rent briefly — am I exempt from the NRL Scheme?
terminals.result_copy: Indicated position: a person who only finds a tenant and collects rent for no more than 3 months may fall within the exemption from operating the NRL Scheme. If rent is collected for more than 3 months, the exemption is not indicated to apply and the scheme obligations are indicated to arise. Review recommended to confirm your specific circumstances.

terminals.heading: I am a letting agent managing a property for a landlord who lives abroad — what must I do?
terminals.result_copy: Indicated position: where you are a letting agent who lives in the UK for more than 6 months a year and you collect rent on behalf of a landlord who lives abroad for more than 6 months of the year, you are indicated to be required to operate the NRL Scheme — deducting basic-rate Income Tax at 20% from the rent, paying it to HMRC within 30 days of the end of each tax quarter, and keeping records for 4 years. Review recommended to confirm your specific circumstances with HMRC.

terminals.heading: When and how do I pay the tax I have deducted under the NRL Scheme?
terminals.result_copy: Indicated position: payment of tax deducted under the NRL Scheme must be sent within 30 days of the end of each tax quarter. The four quarter-end dates are 30 June, 30 September, 31 December, and 31 March. Tax is deducted at the basic rate of 20% on the net rental income. Records must be kept for 4 years. Review recommended to confirm your specific circumstances.

terminals.heading: What records must I keep and for how long?
terminals.result_copy: Indicated position: those operating the NRL Scheme are indicated to be required to keep records for 4 years. This dish states the rule as sourced from the authority — it does not assert your individual outcome. Review recommended to confirm your specific circumstances.

terminals.heading: My landlord lives in the UK — the NRL Scheme does not apply to me
terminals.result_copy: Indicated position: where the landlord lives in the UK for more than 6 months of the year, the NRL Scheme is not indicated to apply. The scheme is triggered only when a landlord lives abroad for more than 6 months of the year. No deduction obligation on the tenant or agent is indicated in this scenario. Review recommended to confirm your specific circumstances.

terminals.heading: Is my landlord abroad long enough to trigger the NRL Scheme?
terminals.result_copy: The NRL Scheme is triggered when a landlord lives abroad for more than 6 months of the year. If you are uncertain whether your landlord meets this threshold, seek confirmation from your landlord or HMRC. If they do meet it and no letting agent is involved, you as tenant may be required to operate the scheme. This dish explains how to determine status and the conditional consequence — it does not assert your individual outcome.

terminals.heading: My landlord is a non-UK company — does the NRL Scheme apply?
terminals.result_copy: Where the landlord is a company or trustee rather than an individual, the rules about their usual place of abode apply in determining whether the NRL Scheme is triggered. The authority source notes this but does not set out the full detail of those rules in the verified facts available. Insufficient information is available here to assert an individual outcome — review recommended and professional or HMRC guidance should be sought.

terminals.heading: What the NRL Scheme is and who it covers
terminals.result_copy: The Non-resident Landlord (NRL) Scheme applies when a landlord lives abroad for more than 6 months of the year. Under the scheme, the responsibility for deducting and paying tax on UK rental income falls on the tenant or letting agent, not the landlord. If the landlord is a company or trustee, the rules about their usual place of abode apply. This dish explains how the scheme works; it does not assert any individual's outcome.

terminals.heading: How do I calculate the tax I owe under the NRL Scheme?
terminals.result_copy: Tax under the NRL Scheme is charged at the basic rate of 20% on the taxable (net) rental amount. For illustration: Julie paid £1,500 rent between 30 June and 30 September, of which £1,200 went directly to her landlord. The taxable amount is £1,300, and 20% of £1,300 gives a payment of £260 due to HMRC. This dish illustrates the calculation method using the verified example from the authority source — it does not assert your individual tax amount.
